content:
Jordan Lee: Kicking off arch review Q&A thread for residency enforcement. Main open items I’m still seeing in docs/PRs:
1) where do we enforce (gateway vs router vs runtime)
2) how do retries behave (client + internal)
3) how does this interact w/ smart routing + fallback

Dropping the current proposal: enforce at gateway admission + repeat checks before any downstream writes. Router must treat pinned region as a hard constraint (no fallback unless explicit override). Want to make sure we’re aligned before ADR-043 final signoff.

(reactions: :eyes: x4)

Ethan Park: +1 on gateway first. From control plane standpoint: if we don’t reject at admission, we risk doing “work” (auth, quota, maybe even model exec) before discovering the region mismatch. That’s both a residency violation + wasted GPU.

But we need to be precise on what data can be generated before residency decision. Even “request metadata in logs” could be out-of-region if gateway is in wrong region.

Amara Diallo: Gateway enforcement is easiest to make deterministic.

My question: are we assuming the customer hits a region-specific base URL (e.g. api.eu-west.redwood.ai) OR do we allow global endpoint + route based on policy?

If global endpoint is allowed, the *first* hop could land in a non-approved region unless we have a geo-aware edge that honors pinned region.

Mina Haddad: Routing side: if policy has `pinned_region=eu-west`, I want router to behave like:
- only consider `eu-west` pools
- do not consider compatible model variant in other regions
- do not do “capacity fallback” cross-region

Otherwise we’re going to have a ton of confusing “sometimes it works” behavior + hard-to-explain compliance posture.

Ravi Menon: +1. Smart routing today does cross-region fallback as a reliability feature. For residency we need it to be opt-in with audit trail.

Maybe we define:
- default when pinned: `allow_cross_region_fallback=false`
- optional override (exception / temporary) that still logs `reason=capacity_exhaustion_override` etc.

Brian Murphy: Error contract Q: if a client hits the US endpoint but org pinned to EU, gateway returns a 4xx.

Two edge cases:
1) SDK retries (esp. for 429/503) could keep hammering wrong endpoint.
2) internal retries between gateway->router->runtime could multiply audit events.

Need guidance: what status + code do we return to ensure clients *don’t* retry blindly, but can remediate (change endpoint/region config).

Marcus Lin: Security perspective: fail-closed is required for enterprise promises.

But we should avoid accidental “silent” violations due to fail-open behavior in policy cache outages. If policy evaluator is down, we deny (with a distinct error code) rather than “best effort route”.

Sean Gallagher: SRE question: if we fail closed when policy service is unreachable, that’s a new availability dependency. Fine, but we need:
- clear alarms on policy evaluator errors
- runbook for “policy evaluator degraded => increased 403/503?”

Also please do NOT make it a tight synchronous call on every request with no caching.

Jordan Lee: On endpoints: current thinking from product is regional endpoints are the primary supported way for Hosted/Dedicated (and console will show the right base URL when pinned).

Global endpoint story is TBD. If we keep `api.redwood.ai` as an alias, it must still land in the allowed region at the edge. If we can’t guarantee that, we should document: “when pinned, you must use the region base URL”.

Amara Diallo: +1. From gateway implementation: we can do the region check based on:
- `request_region` (where this gateway instance is running)
- `desired_region` (from host / optional header)
- policy output (allowed/pinned)

Pseudo:
```
if pinned_region && request_region != pinned_region:
  deny RESIDENCY_REGION_MISMATCH
```

But this assumes the request even makes it to the EU gateway when pinned=EU. If customer hits US hostname, it’ll go to US gateway and we deny there (which is OK, but means request metadata got processed in US). Need to define if that “counts” as a violation.

Marcus Lin: Good catch. “In-scope data” includes request metadata + logs. If a pinned EU customer sends a request to US gateway, even reading headers/body in US is arguably out-of-region processing.

But: we can’t stop customers from sending packets to the wrong place. We can only ensure we don’t *persist* their payload and don’t execute inference.

So we should message it as: request is rejected at admission; no model execution; no downstream writes; minimal transient processing to return error.

Brian Murphy: +1. We should be explicit in docs/error payload:
- “Your request was rejected before model execution due to residency policy.”
- “Use the EU endpoint or set SDK region=eu-west.”

Also status code: I vote 403 (policy violation) not 400. And we set `Retry-After: 0`? (not a thing) but at least don’t use 503.

Mina Haddad: For router retries: we currently retry on certain upstream errors and can do pool re-selection.

When pinned, pool re-selection must stay within region. That part is straightforward.

But we also have “fallback to other region” codepath in reliability. We need to gate it behind `allow_cross_region_fallback` and have it default false when pinned.

Elena Popov: Implementation note: router’s selection algorithm takes a list of candidate clusters. Today that list can include cross-region if SLO policy says “prefer local, but allow nearest”.

For pinned, we can make the candidate list builder enforce region constraint at the top (before scoring). Then no further code needs to “remember” residency.

Victor Alvarez: Network constraints: if we allow cross-region override, we need to ensure:
- cross-region connectivity exists (some regions have restricted peering)
- and if it’s enabled, it’s still auditable + explicit.

So please don’t implement a “silent fallback” even if it would work technically.

Sean Gallagher: Re: retries + audit spam. Can we make audit event emission:
- at decision point (gateway) once per request id
- and in router only when decision differs? (shouldn’t)

Otherwise internal retries could flood SIEM exports.

Ethan Park: We can use a stable `request_id` and emit:
- `residency.policy_evaluated` at gateway with decision allow/deny
- `residency.violation` only on deny

Internal components can tag traces with `residency_decision=allow` but not emit separate audit events unless a downstream write is blocked.

Jordan Lee: +1. Separate “audit logs” vs “telemetry logs”. We can keep high-cardinality metrics/traces in region, but audit events should be minimal + deduped.

Brian Murphy: On HTTP codes:
- Region mismatch (wrong endpoint/SDK region): 403 + `RESIDENCY_REGION_MISMATCH`
- Policy evaluator unavailable (can’t determine): 503 + `RESIDENCY_POLICY_UNAVAILABLE`? (or 500)

But careful: 503 will be retried by SDKs. If policy is down, retries might be ok (transient). For mismatch, definitely no retries.

Amara Diallo: Agree. Gateway can set `x-redwood-retryable: false` for mismatch, `true` for policy unavailable. SDKs can key off that.

Also we can return machine-readable `remediation` fields:
- `expected_region`
- `request_region`
- `docs_url`

Marcus Lin: Remediation fields are great but double-check we’re not echoing sensitive config. Region is fine.

Also: when we do explicit cross-region override, we need audit event to include:
- who/what enabled it (exception id)
- expiry
- reason

Sean Gallagher: For policy cache failures: what’s the plan if gateway cache is stale and policy changed to more restrictive? That’s the scary case.

Ethan Park: Proposed cache rule: “stale allowed decisions are not safe”.

So:
- cache TTL short (e.g., 60s)
- if cache entry expired and policy evaluator unreachable => deny with `RESIDENCY_POLICY_UNAVAILABLE`
- if cache entry fresh, use it

Plus we’ll push config via streaming to reduce dependency on synchronous calls.

Mina Haddad: Router side can take policy as part of request context from gateway (signed/validated) so router doesn’t call policy service at all. That reduces variability.

Jordan Lee: OK, summarizing decisions for ADR-043 draft:
- Enforcement points:
  - admission: API gateway MUST enforce pinned/allowed regions before model execution
  - router MUST constrain candidates to allowed/pinned region; cross-region fallback disabled by default when pinned
  - downstream writes MUST enforce (analytics/log persistence/etc) as a backstop
- Endpoint behavior:
  - pinned customers should use region-specific base URL; if they hit wrong region, gateway denies; minimal transient processing only
- Retry behavior:
  - mismatch is non-retryable (403 + RESIDENCY_REGION_MISMATCH)
  - policy unavailable is retryable (503 + RESIDENCY_POLICY_UNAVAILABLE)
  - internal retries must not generate duplicate audit events; use request_id + emit audit at gateway only

If anyone objects, please reply here by EOD.

Architecture Bot: Reminder: ADR-043 review meeting tomorrow 11:00–11:30 PT. Doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ARCH/ADR-043-residency-enforcement-at-gateway

(reactions: :thumbsup: x6)

Neha Kapoor: No objections. Please add one line in ADR about “fail closed for residency checks” so it’s unambiguous.

Marcus Lin: +1. Also call out that cross-region override requires GRC-approved exception (link to exception process) so it’s not treated as an SRE knob.

Jordan Lee: Got it. Will update ADR text + link exception process section. Closing thread unless new issues come up.
